questions.scenario: Your society is organizing a winter clothes collection drive (like Goonj) for the homeless. What is your main task?

options.text: Physically lifting the heavy gunny bags of clothes, sorting the jackets from the sweaters, and packing them tightly.
Keeping a register to count exactly how many blankets were collected versus how many are actually needed.
Designing an emotional WhatsApp forward with a catchy Hindi slogan to encourage more aunties to donate.
Convincing the society secretary to place a permanent drop-box at the main gate for year-round donations.

questions.scenario: You want to help the stray dogs in your colony. How do you go about it?

options.text: Going out every evening with packets of Parle-G or leftover roti to physically feed them and pat them.
Keeping a notebook tracking which dog got their anti-rabies shot and noticing patterns in their health.
Taking cute, aesthetic videos of the puppies and making an Instagram reel to find them good homes.
Collecting Rs. 50 a month from dog-loving neighbors to buy bulk Pedigree and fund their vaccinations.

questions.scenario: It's the 'Joy of Giving' week at school. Your class is in charge of the donation drive. What's your role?

options.text: Loading the heavy cartons of rice, dal, and old toys onto the school bus to deliver to the orphanage.
Cross-checking the inventory lists to make sure every class successfully met their minimum donation quota.
Decorating the cardboard donation boxes with colorful chart paper and beautiful calligraphy.
Giving a powerful speech in the morning assembly to motivate the junior kids to donate more than last year.

questions.scenario: There is a massive Blood Donation Camp happening in your society's clubhouse. How are you helping?

options.text: Running around handing out Frooti and biscuits to the donors who feel dizzy after giving blood.
Sitting at the registration desk, making sure donor weights, blood groups, and hemoglobin levels are recorded perfectly.
Clicking great photos of the donors and making 'Thank You' digital certificates for the society WhatsApp group.
Talking to the hospital authorities to negotiate free basic health checkups for everyone who donates.

questions.scenario: You are volunteering at a local Gurudwara Langar or temple Bhandara. Where are you most active?

options.text: Walking down the rows with the heavy steel buckets, serving hot poori and sabzi directly to the people.
Estimating how many kilos of atta and liters of oil will be needed so the kitchen doesn't run out of food.
Filming a beautiful, cinematic video of the massive cooking process with a soulful background track.
Approaching local grocery shop owners (Sethji) and convincing them to sponsor the raw materials for the week.

questions.scenario: Your maid's daughter is struggling with her studies. How do you support her?

options.text: Sitting with her on the floor every evening and patiently teaching her Math and English yourself.
Looking at her past report cards to pinpoint her weakest subjects and finding free YouTube channels for her.
Giving her your colorful gel pens, sketch pens, and drawing books to make the learning process fun and visual.
Talking to your school principal to see if she can get admission under the RTE (Right to Education) quota.

questions.scenario: During the heavy monsoons, the nearby slum area gets totally flooded. What is your first instinct?

options.text: Putting on a raincoat, grabbing a stick, and physically helping the locals clear the choked drains.
Researching why the municipal drainage failed this year and mapping out the most affected lanes.
Taking powerful, heartbreaking photos of the waterlogged huts and tweeting them to the local MLA.
Mobilizing your tuition friends to pool their pocket money so you can buy emergency tarpaulin sheets.

questions.scenario: You see a massive pile of garbage burning in an empty plot next to your house. What do you do?

options.text: Quickly grab buckets of water and sand from your house and try to extinguish the toxic fire yourself.
Check the Air Quality Index (AQI) app on your phone and find the exact government helpline to report it.
Make a sarcastic poster about 'Swachh Bharat' with a picture of the fire and post it on the RWA group.
Confront the people burning it and demand the RWA officially hires a private waste collection auto.

questions.scenario: Your school plans to plant 100 trees on Environment Day. What is your contribution?

options.text: Digging the hard soil with a trowel, planting the saplings, and getting your hands completely muddy.
Researching which native Indian trees (like Neem or Peepal) will actually survive the local summer heat.
Painting the clay pots with bright traditional designs so the plantation drive looks festive and vibrant.
Convincing the local nursery owner to donate 50 saplings for free in exchange for putting up their banner.

questions.scenario: When you hear about a major crisis (like a flood or earthquake in another state) on the news, what do you naturally want to do?

options.text: Wish you were old enough to pack your bags, travel to the site, and join the rescue teams pulling people out.
Read articles to understand the geographical cause of the disaster and how many exact villages were impacted.
Share powerful infographics on your Instagram story to make sure your friends don't ignore the tragedy.
Set up a UPI QR code at your society's gate and start collecting funds to send to the Chief Minister's Relief Fund.

Field_Relief_Worker.title: The Ground Hero (Field Relief Worker / Volunteer)
Field_Relief_Worker.primary_match_text: You are highly empathetic, active, and hands-on. You don't just talk about helping people; you get your hands dirty and do the actual physical work required to make a difference.
Field_Relief_Worker.day_in_the_life: Traveling to rural villages, directly distributing food and medical supplies, rescuing animals, and working face-to-face with people who need immediate help.
Field_Relief_Worker.alternative_match_text: Your action-oriented empathy would also make you a fantastic Nurse, Disaster Management Responder, or Special Educator.
Field_Relief_Worker.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Humanities is great). Degree: Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) or BA in Sociology. Next Steps: Pursue an MSW (Master of Social Work) from top institutes like TISS or work directly with grassroots NGOs.

Impact_Analyst.title: The Data Detective (NGO Impact Analyst / Researcher)
Impact_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are logical, detail-oriented, and rely on facts. You know that to truly solve poverty or hunger, we need to understand the root cause, track the data, and measure what actually works.
Impact_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Surveying villages to collect health data, writing detailed research reports for the government, and calculating if an NGO's money is actually changing lives.
Impact_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your love for facts and social impact makes you a perfect fit for Public Policy Analysis, Economics, or Data Science.
Impact_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Humanities (with Math/Economics). Degree: BA in Economics, Statistics, or Sociology. Next Steps: Master's in Public Policy (MPP) or Development Studies from universities like Azim Premji University.

Campaign_Designer.title: The Voice of the Cause (Campaign & Communications Designer)
Campaign_Designer.primary_match_text: You are a creative storyteller. You understand that to get people to care about a social issue, you have to touch their hearts through powerful videos, posters, and stories.
Campaign_Designer.day_in_the_life: Visiting tribal areas to film documentaries, managing the Instagram pages for big charities, and designing viral campaigns that raise awareness for human rights.
Campaign_Designer.alternative_match_text: With your massive creativity, you would also excel in Journalism, Digital Marketing, or Documentary Filmmaking.
Campaign_Designer.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream. Degree: BA in Mass Communication, Journalism, or Bachelor of Design (B.Des). Next Steps: Build a strong digital portfolio and intern with media teams of organizations like UNICEF or CRY.

NGO_Director.title: The Chief Organizer (NGO Director / Fundraising Manager)
NGO_Director.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader with a business mind, but you want to use your skills for good. You know how to convince people, manage teams, and raise the massive funds required to run a charity.
NGO_Director.day_in_the_life: Meeting CEOs of huge companies to ask for CSR (Corporate Social Responsibility) funds, managing a team of 50 volunteers, and expanding the NGO to new cities.
NGO_Director.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and negotiation skills would also make you an incredible Corporate CEO, PR Director, or Politician.
NGO_Director.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Humanities. Degree: BBA, B.Com, or BSW. Next Steps: Pursue an MBA in Rural/Social Management (from IRMA) or a Master of Social Work (MSW) to lead large-scale organizations.
